observations.expected: Two large upper abdominal gas lucencies represent a larger stomach on the patient left and proximal duodenum on the right.
observations.observed: Two large gas lucencies are visible in the upper abdomen. The larger one is on the patient's left (stomach) and a second, somewhat smaller lucency is on the patient's right (proximal duodenum), consistent with the classic 'double bubble' sign of duodenal atresia.

observations.expected: Little or no gas is visible distal to the two bubbles within this cropped field.
observations.observed: No bowel gas is visible distal to the two gas collections in the remainder of the abdomen. The lower abdomen appears gasless, consistent with complete obstruction at the duodenum.

observations.expected: Visible skeletal proportions are compatible with a newborn.
observations.observed: The ribs are thin and horizontally oriented, the vertebral bodies show immature ossification with rounded margins, and the overall skeletal proportions are consistent with a newborn or young infant. No mature ossification centers or degenerative changes are present.
